name: La Villa

pitch_detail.notes: Approach scramble shared with the Southeast Face to reach the base of the summit block.
The dihedral on the taller summit spire: ~2/3 easier 5.6 climbing, a solid cam placement, then three slabby 5.8 crux moves, a jug pull, and 5.5 to a large belay ledge ~10 ft left of the true summit.

rappels: Single ~40 ft (12 m) rappel from the fixed sling/horn anchor at the shared, heavily-slung top-out area near the Southeast Face finish.
descent_text: From the belay ledge atop La Villa, traverse rightward (climber's right) past the true summit to the heavily-trafficked low-5th topout area shared with the Southeast Face route, where fixed slings are typically already in place. Make a single ~40 ft (12 m) rappel back to the base of the technical section, downclimb the 3rd-class terrain below, and reverse the scree traverse and Pinnacle Peak Trail back to Reflection Lakes.
approach: Same as the Southeast Face: from Reflection Lakes (4,859 ft), take the Pinnacle Peak Trail 1.3 miles to the Pinnacle–Plummer saddle, then contour across Pinnacle's south-face scree/talus to the base of Castle's southeast side and scramble up broken ground to reach the base of the summit block. During the Plummer Peak Fire the park closed the Butter Creek Research Natural Area, south of the Pinnacle Peak Trail to the park boundary; its edge runs along the crest at The Castle, so Castle's south side and the east end of this traverse are off limits while that closure stands. Check the park's fire and closure notices before you go.
overview: A three-star, low-fifth-class trad line in the small rock-climbing area on The Castle, distinct from (and reportedly higher quality than) the standard scramble/chimney route to the summit.
beta: A 5.7 trad route in The Castle's climbing area alongside the easy-5th-class Southeast Face; no detailed pitch-by-pitch description, approach specifics, or first-ascent history is on record. Likely approached the same way as the Southeast Face — via the Pinnacle Peak Trail from Reflection Lakes and a traverse across Pinnacle's south-face scree to the Castle-Pinnacle area.
face: Southeast Face, summit block — dihedral on the taller of the two summit spires, left of the Southeast Face line
